findings: R1 concurrent accepts can destroy a live join
R2 startup reconciliation can drop a valid invitation after an interrupted restore
remediation_round_1.code: R1: joinGroupFromWelcomeCore now runs check -> destroy -> join -> saveGroup (and the already-joined short-circuit) inside withGroupJoinLock(groupId). That uses navigator.locks.request('few-join-<groupId>') when available (the cross-tab guarantee), else a per-groupId in-module promise chain. A rejected run does not wedge the chain. An unresolvable id takes no lock. R2: dropInvitationsForJoinedGroups(marmotClient) drops an invitation only when an overlay record exists AND groups.has(groupId) is true; a has() failure keeps it. New loadGroupsAndReconcileInvitations(client) replaces MarmotContext's loadAll block, skips reconciliation when loadAll fails, and never throws. Also: the groups-accept-reload-atomic header now states it cannot pick a cut point (the unit tests cover each branch); the docs/behavior/groups.md wording on the brief overlap was softened.

root_cause: Accepting a Welcome writes two stores non-atomically: marmot-ts joinGroupFromWelcome persists MLS state (few-groups-state), then the app saves the overlay Group (few-groups-meta), then dequeues the invitation. An unload between the writes, or a leave (leaveGroupImpl purges only the overlay), leaves MLS state without an overlay. Any later join of that group hits adoptClientState's 'Group <hex> already exists'; acceptPendingInvitation's catch then drops the invitation as 'no longer valid'. So re-invite after leave always failed, and an interrupted accept left the user an invisible MLS member. An unload after saveGroup but before the dequeue left a joined card plus a stale invitation.
fix: joinGroupFromWelcomeCore (shared by manual accept and auto-accept) resolves the group id pre-join: the pending entry's groupId, else readPreJoinGroupData -> readWelcomeGroupInfo groupContext.groupId, never the rumor pubkey. If marmotClient.groups.has(id): with an overlay record it returns the existing Group without joining (already joined); without one it calls await marmotClient.groups.destroy(id), a local-only purge, then joins normally. An unresolvable id skips the check. The existing catch stays as the last resort. New export dropInvitationsForJoinedGroups() runs in MarmotContext init right after groups.loadAll(). It drops pending invitations whose non-empty groupId has an overlay record and leaves legacy empty-groupId entries alone. No publishes were added.
